title: An integral quasi-coherent algebra on a qcqs scheme is a directed colimit of finite (and finitely presented) quasi-coherent algebras
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. A *quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra* is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras whose underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]; it is *finite* (resp. *integral*, resp. *of finite presentation*) if for every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ the $R$-algebra $\mathcal A(U)$ is finite, i.e. finitely generated as an $R$-module (resp. integral, i.e. every element is a root of a monic polynomial over $R$; resp. of finite presentation, i.e. isomorphic to $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(g_1,\dots,g_m)$). Let $\mathcal A$ be an integral quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra. Then (1) $\mathcal A$ is the directed colimit of its finite quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-subalgebras (these form a directed set under inclusion, and the inclusions induce an isomorphism from their colimit to $\mathcal A$); and (2) there exist a directed set $I$, a system $(\mathcal A_i,\varphi_{i'i}:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A_{i'})_{i\le i'}$ over $I$ of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebras each of which is finite and of finite presentation, and $\mathcal O_X$-algebra maps $\varphi_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A$ with $\varphi_{i'}\circ\varphi_{i'i}=\varphi_i$, which induce an isomorphism $\varinjlim_i\mathcal A_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal A$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] (colimit in the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras, equivalently of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebras). The maps $\varphi_i$ need not be injective.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 0817 (lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite, line 3424; proof lines 3436-3496, via Lemma 05JT lemma-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-type (line 3349), Lemma 01PK lemma-directed-colimit-finite-presentation (line 3193), Modules Lemma 01BS lemma-finite-presentation-quasi-compact-colimit, Algebra Lemma 02JJ lemma-characterize-finite-in-terms-of-integral, and the proofs of Lemmas 05JS (line 3297) and 086N lemma-finite-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-finitely-presented (line 3378)); the definitions of finite/integral/finitely presented quasi-coherent algebras at lines 3289-3293 and 3369-3374

proof.text: *Step 1 (for subalgebras of $\mathcal A$, finite = of finite type).* Let $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal A$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-subalgebra (a subsheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-subalgebras, quasi-coherent as a module; the notion of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-type]). If $\mathcal B$ is finite, then for every affine open $U$ a finite set of $\mathcal O_X(U)$-module generators of $\mathcal B(U)$ also generates it as an $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra, so $\mathcal B$ is of finite type. Conversely let $\mathcal B$ be of finite type and $U\subseteq X$ affine open, $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$; let $b_1,\dots,b_m$ generate $\mathcal B(U)$ as an $R$-algebra. Since $\mathcal B(U)\subseteq\mathcal A(U)$ is an $R$-subalgebra and $\mathcal A(U)$ is integral over $R$ ($\mathcal A$ is integral), each $b_l$ is a root of a monic polynomial over $R$, and this equation holds in $\mathcal B(U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] (Algebra 02JJ, (3)$\Rightarrow$(1)) $\mathcal B(U)$ is a finitely generated $R$-module. So $\mathcal B$ is finite. Hence the finite quasi-coherent subalgebras of $\mathcal A$ are exactly its quasi-coherent subalgebras of finite type.

source.place: Properties, proof of Lemma 0817, first paragraph (lines 3437-3442: 'Any finite type quasi-coherent O_X-subalgebra of A is finite (apply Algebra, Lemma 02JJ to A_i(U) in A(U) for affine opens U)')

proof.text: *Step 2 (proof of (1)).* By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-type] (Properties 05JT; $X$ is qcqs and $\mathcal A$ quasi-coherent) the set $\Sigma$ of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-subalgebras of finite type of $\mathcal A$, ordered by inclusion, is directed, and the inclusions induce an isomorphism $\varinjlim_{\mathcal B\in\Sigma}\mathcal B\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal A$ in sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras (equivalently in quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebras, a full subcategory containing all terms). By Step 1, $\Sigma$ is exactly the set of finite quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-subalgebras of $\mathcal A$. This is (1).

source.place: Properties, proof of Lemma 0817, first paragraph (lines 3436-3442)

proof.text: *Step 3 (setup for (2): $\mathcal A$ as a colimit of finitely presented modules, symmetric algebras, kernels).* By [lem-weil-pbc-module-directed-colimit-finite-presentation] (Properties 01PK) applied to the underlying quasi-coherent module of $\mathcal A$ there are a directed set $I$, a system $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i})$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules of finite presentation and $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\varphi_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal A$, $\varphi_{i'}\varphi_{i'i}=\varphi_i$, with $(\mathcal A,(\varphi_i))=\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i$ in $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Modules of finite presentation are quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](0), so [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] gives quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebras $\mathcal S_i:=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F_i)$ with $j_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal S_i$; by its part (a) let $\psi_i:\mathcal S_i\to\mathcal A$ be the algebra map with $\psi_i j_i=\varphi_i$ and, for $i\le i'$, $\sigma_{i'i}=\operatorname{Sym}(\varphi_{i'i}):\mathcal S_i\to\mathcal S_{i'}$ the algebra map with $\sigma_{i'i}j_i=j_{i'}\varphi_{i'i}$. By the uniqueness in (a): $\sigma_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $\sigma_{i''i'}\sigma_{i'i}=\sigma_{i''i}$, and $\psi_{i'}\sigma_{i'i}=\psi_i$ (both restrict to $\varphi_{i'}\varphi_{i'i}=\varphi_i$ along $j_i$). Let $\mathcal J_i=\ker\psi_i$, a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal S_i$ with $\mathcal J_i(U)=\ker\psi_{i,U}$ on affine opens [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-kernel-image-ideal](a). From $\psi_{i'}\sigma_{i'i}=\psi_i$, $\sigma_{i'i}(\mathcal J_i)\subseteq\mathcal J_{i'}$.

source.place: Properties, proof of Lemma 0817, second paragraph (lines 3446-3457: 'write A = colim F_i ... using Lemma 01PK. For each i let J_i be the kernel of Sym*(F_i) -> A. For i' >= i there is an induced map J_i -> J_i''), with the symmetric algebra and the kernel as in the proof of Lemma 05JS (lines 3320-3326)

proof.text: *Step 4 (the image $\mathcal A'_i=\operatorname{Im}\psi_i\cong\mathcal S_i/\mathcal J_i$ is finite).* By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-kernel-image-ideal](a) $\mathcal A'_i:=\operatorname{Im}\psi_i$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-subalgebra of $\mathcal A$ with $\mathcal A'_i(U)=\psi_{i,U}(\mathcal S_i(U))$ for affine $U$, $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra](b) $\mathcal S_i(U)=\operatorname{Sym}_R(\mathcal F_i(U))$, and $\mathcal F_i(U)$ is a finitely presented, in particular finitely generated, $R$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](b); by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-finite-presentation](a) $\mathcal S_i(U)$, hence its image $\mathcal A'_i(U)$, is a finitely generated $R$-algebra. So $\mathcal A'_i$ is of finite type, hence finite by Step 1. (Stacks: 'the quasi-coherent O_X-algebras Sym*(F_i)/J_i are finite (see above)'.)

source.place: Properties, proof of Lemma 0817, second paragraph (lines 3458-3460), with the proof of Lemma 05JT (lines 3367-3369: the images are quasi-coherent subalgebras of finite type)

proof.text: *Step 5 (the finitely presented algebras $\mathcal A_{ik}$).* Fix $i$. $\mathcal J_i$ is quasi-coherent, so by [lem-weil-pbc-module-directed-colimit-finite-presentation] there are a directed set $K_i$, a system $(\mathcal E_{ik})_{k\in K_i}$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules of finite presentation with transition maps $\eta_{k'k}$, and $\varepsilon_{ik}:\mathcal E_{ik}\to\mathcal J_i$ with $\varepsilon_{ik'}\eta_{k'k}=\varepsilon_{ik}$ and $(\mathcal J_i,(\varepsilon_{ik}))=\varinjlim_k\mathcal E_{ik}$. Let $e_{ik}:\mathcal E_{ik}\to\mathcal S_i$ be $\varepsilon_{ik}$ followed by $\mathcal J_i\subseteq\mathcal S_i$, $\mathcal I_{ik}:=(e_{ik}(\mathcal E_{ik}))\subseteq\mathcal S_i$ the sheaf of ideals it generates and $q_{ik}:\mathcal S_i\to\mathcal A_{ik}:=\mathcal S_i/\mathcal I_{ik}$ the quotient, both quasi-coherent with $\mathcal I_{ik}(U)=$ the ideal generated by $e_{ik,U}(\mathcal E_{ik}(U))$ and $\mathcal A_{ik}(U)=\mathcal S_i(U)/\mathcal I_{ik}(U)$ for affine $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-kernel-image-ideal](b). Since $\mathcal J_i$ is a sheaf of ideals containing $e_{ik}(\mathcal E_{ik})$, $\mathcal I_{ik}\subseteq\mathcal J_i$; so $\psi_i$ kills $e_{ik}$ and factors uniquely as $\pi_{ik}q_{ik}$ with $\pi_{ik}:\mathcal A_{ik}\to\mathcal A$ (universal property in (b)). For $k\le k'$, $e_{ik}=e_{ik'}\eta_{k'k}$ gives $\mathcal I_{ik}\subseteq\mathcal I_{ik'}$. Each $\mathcal A_{ik}$ is of finite presentation: for affine $U$, $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $\mathcal S_i(U)=\operatorname{Sym}_R(\mathcal F_i(U))$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra](b) with $\mathcal F_i(U)$ finitely presented and $\mathcal E_{ik}(U)$ finitely generated over $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](b), so $\mathcal I_{ik}(U)$ is generated by the images of finitely many generators of $\mathcal E_{ik}(U)$, and $\mathcal A_{ik}(U)=\operatorname{Sym}_R(\mathcal F_i(U))/\mathcal I_{ik}(U)$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-finite-presentation](b).

source.place: Properties, proof of Lemma 0817, second paragraph (lines 3460-3462 'Write J_i = colim E_ik as a colimit of finitely presented O_X-modules', and lines 3474-3484: A_ik = Sym*(F_i)/(E_ik), 'of finite presentation'), with the proof of Lemma 05JS (lines 3326-3333)

proof.text: *Step 6 (the directed index set $P$ and the system).* Let $P=\{(i,k):i\in I,k\in K_i\}$ with $(i,k)\le(i',k')$ iff $i\le i'$ and $\sigma_{i'i}(\mathcal I_{ik})\subseteq\mathcal I_{i'k'}$ (the order of Stacks 05JS, which the proof of 0817 leaves implicit). It is reflexive and transitive since $\sigma_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\sigma_{i''i'}\sigma_{i'i}=\sigma_{i''i}$. Note $\sigma_{i'i}(\mathcal I_{ik})\subseteq\mathcal I_{i'k'}$ as soon as $\sigma_{i'i}e_{ik}$ factors through $\mathcal I_{i'k'}$ (the preimage $\sigma_{i'i}^{-1}(\mathcal I_{i'k'})$ is a sheaf of ideals containing $e_{ik}(\mathcal E_{ik})$). For $(i,k)\le(i',k')$, $q_{i'k'}\sigma_{i'i}$ kills $e_{ik}$, so it factors uniquely as $\alpha_{(i'k'),(ik)}q_{ik}$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-kernel-image-ideal](b); by uniqueness these transition maps compose and $\pi_{i'k'}\alpha=\pi_{ik}$ (from $\psi_{i'}\sigma_{i'i}=\psi_i$). Directedness (Stacks: 'Given i' >= i and k there exists a k' ... This follows from Modules, Lemma 01BS'): $P\neq\emptyset$ as $I$ and the $K_i$ are nonempty. Given $(i_1,k_1),(i_2,k_2)$ choose $i'\ge i_1,i_2$. For $a=1,2$ the map $\sigma_{i'i_a}\varepsilon_{i_ak_a}:\mathcal E_{i_ak_a}\to\mathcal J_{i'}$ (it lands in $\mathcal J_{i'}$ by Step 3) goes from a module of finite presentation into $\varinjlim_k\mathcal E_{i'k}$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-hom-directed-colimit] (Modules 01BS; $X$ qcqs) it equals $\varepsilon_{i'k_a'}g_a$ for some $k_a'\in K_{i'}$ and $g_a$. Take $k'\ge k_1',k_2'$ in $K_{i'}$; then $\sigma_{i'i_a}e_{i_ak_a}=e_{i'k'}\eta_{k'k_a'}g_a$ factors through $\mathcal I_{i'k'}$, so $(i_a,k_a)\le(i',k')$.

source.place: Properties, proof of Lemma 0817, second paragraph (lines 3463-3484: the commutative square E_ik -> E_i'k' over J_i -> J_i', Modules Lemma 01BS, and the induced map A_ik -> A_i'k'); the order on pairs from the proof of Lemma 05JS (lines 3334-3336)

proof.text: *Step 7 ($\varinjlim_{P}\mathcal A_{ik}=\mathcal A$).* By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-colimit] the colimit $(\mathcal L,(\lambda_{ik}))$ of the system $(\mathcal A_{ik})_P$ exists in quasi-coherent (equivalently, all sheaves of) $\mathcal O_X$-algebras, with $\mathcal L(U)=\varinjlim_P\mathcal A_{ik}(U)$ for affine $U$; let $\pi:\mathcal L\to\mathcal A$ be induced by the $\pi_{ik}$. Fix an affine open $U$. Surjectivity of $\pi_U$: by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-colimit-affine-sections] for $\mathcal A=\varinjlim\mathcal F_i$, every $a\in\mathcal A(U)$ is $\varphi_{i,U}(x)$ with $x\in\mathcal F_i(U)$; then $a=\psi_{i,U}(j_{i,U}(x))=\pi_{ik,U}(q_{ik,U}(j_{i,U}(x)))$ for any $k\in K_i$. Injectivity: by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise](2) an element of $\mathcal L(U)$ is $\lambda_{ik,U}(y)$ with $y\in\mathcal A_{ik}(U)$; suppose $\pi_{ik,U}(y)=0$. Write $y=q_{ik,U}(z)$, $z\in\mathcal S_i(U)$ ($q_{ik,U}$ is surjective on affines, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-kernel-image-ideal](b)). Then $\psi_{i,U}(z)=0$, so $z\in\mathcal J_i(U)$ (part (a)), and by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-colimit-affine-sections] for $\mathcal J_i=\varinjlim_k\mathcal E_{ik}$, $z=\varepsilon_{ik',U}(w)$ for some $k'$ and $w\in\mathcal E_{ik'}(U)$, so $z\in\mathcal I_{ik'}(U)$. Choose $k''\ge k,k'$ in $K_i$: $(i,k)\le(i,k'')$ (as $\mathcal I_{ik}\subseteq\mathcal I_{ik''}$) and $z\in\mathcal I_{ik''}(U)$, so $\alpha_{(ik''),(ik)}(y)=q_{ik'',U}(z)=0$ and $\lambda_{ik,U}(y)=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-rings-zero]. So $\pi_U$ is bijective for every affine $U$; the affine opens form a basis, so $\pi$ is an isomorphism of sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis](b), and its inverse is an algebra map. (Stacks: 'colim A_ik = colim A_i = A ... the first equality was shown in the proof of Lemma 086N and the second because A is the colimit of the modules F_i'.)

source.place: Properties, proof of Lemma 0817, last sentences (lines 3488-3495), referring to the proof of Lemma 086N (lines 3400-3407: A = colim Sym*(F)/(E_i) since J = colim E_i)

proof.text: *Step 8 (finiteness for $k$ large: the cofinal subset $P_{\rm fin}$).* Fix $i$. As $X$ is quasi-compact choose an affine open covering $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_m$, $R_j=\mathcal O_X(U_j)$, and generators $f_{j,1},\dots,f_{j,N_j}$ of the finitely generated $R_j$-module $\mathcal F_i(U_j)$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine]. By Step 4, $\mathcal A'_i(U_j)$ is a finite $R_j$-algebra, hence integral [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]: there are monic $P_{j,l}\in R_j[T]$ with $P_{j,l}(\psi_{i,U_j}(j_i(f_{j,l})))=0$, i.e. $z_{j,l}:=P_{j,l}(j_i(f_{j,l}))\in\ker\psi_{i,U_j}=\mathcal J_i(U_j)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-colimit-affine-sections] each $z_{j,l}$ lies in $e_{ik}(\mathcal E_{ik}(U_j))$ for some $k$, and since $K_i$ is directed and the $\mathcal I_{ik}$ increase with $k$ there is $k_0(i)\in K_i$ with all (finitely many) $z_{j,l}\in\mathcal I_{ik_0(i)}(U_j)$. For $k\ge k_0(i)$ in $K_i$: in $\mathcal A_{ik}(U_j)=\mathcal S_i(U_j)/\mathcal I_{ik}(U_j)$ the images of the $f_{j,l}$ satisfy the monic $P_{j,l}$, and they generate it as an $R_j$-algebra ([lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra](b) and [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-finite-presentation](a)); so $\mathcal A_{ik}(U_j)$ is a finite $R_j$-module [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] for every $j$, hence by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](c) $\mathcal A_{ik}(U)$ is finitely generated over $\mathcal O_X(U)$ for every affine open $U$: $\mathcal A_{ik}$ is finite. Let $P_{\rm fin}=\{(i,k)\in P:k\ge k_0(i)\text{ in }K_i\}$. It is cofinal in $P$: for $(i,k)\in P$ take $k''\ge k,k_0(i)$; then $(i,k)\le(i,k'')\in P_{\rm fin}$. It is directed: two elements have an upper bound $(i',k')$ in $P$ (Step 6), and $(i',k')\le(i',k'')\in P_{\rm fin}$ for $k''\ge k',k_0(i')$.

source.place: Properties, proof of Lemma 0817 ('The quasi-coherent O_X-algebras A_ik are of finite presentation and finite for k large enough (see proof of Lemma 086N)', lines 3484-3487), with the proof of Lemma 086N (lines 3407-3420: finite affine covering, generators f_jk, monic P_jk, P_jk(f_jk) = 0 in A_i(U_j) for i large)

proof.text: *Step 9 (conclusion of (2)).* View the directed preordered sets $P\supseteq P_{\rm fin}$ as filtered categories; $P^{\rm op}$ is cofiltered, $P_{\rm fin}^{\rm op}$ is a full subcategory, and by Step 8 every object of $P$ maps to an object of $P_{\rm fin}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory](1) (applied to $\mathcal I=P^{\rm op}$, $\mathcal J=P_{\rm fin}^{\rm op}$ and the diagram $(\mathcal A_{ik})$ in sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras) the canonical map $\varinjlim_{P_{\rm fin}}\mathcal A_{ik}\to\varinjlim_P\mathcal A_{ik}$ is an isomorphism, and by Step 7 the latter is $\mathcal A$ via the $\pi_{ik}$. So the directed set $P_{\rm fin}$, the system $(\mathcal A_{ik},\alpha)$ of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebras, each finite (Step 8) and of finite presentation (Step 5), and the maps $\pi_{ik}$ satisfy (2) [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; the colimit is the same in quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebras [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-colimit]. The $\pi_{ik}$ need not be injective (a finitely presented $\mathcal A_{ik}$ can have a nonzero kernel to $\mathcal A$).

lean.statement: theorem integral_algebra_directed_colimit_finite (X : Scheme.{v}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (A : QuasiCoherentAlgebra X) (hA : A.obj.IsIntegral) : (Nonempty A.FiniteSubalgebras ∧ IsDirected A.FiniteSubalgebras (· ≤ ·) ∧ ∃ (c : Cocone A.finiteSubalgebraDiagram) (e : c.pt ≅ A.obj), (∀ B : A.FiniteSubalgebras, c.ι.app B ≫ e.hom = B.val.arrow) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit c)) ∧ (∃ (I : Type v) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)) (F : I ⥤ QuasiCoherentAlgebra X) (c : Cocone (F ⋙ (X.IsQuasiCoherentAlgebra).ι)) (e : c.pt ≅ A.obj), (∀ i : I, (F.obj i).obj.IsFinite ∧ (F.obj i).obj.IsFinitePresentation) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit c))
